title: Ant Bailing Open-Sources Ling-3.2-air, Breaking Through the Deployment Bottleneck of Complex Workflows with 5.5 Billion Activated Parameters

content_html:
In the deep end of putting AI coding and agents into production, developers face a common awkward reality: models shine at simple code completion, but once they are dropped into real, complex code repositories or multi-step automation workflows, they often fail to live up to their apparent promise, break down logically, and hallucinate frequently. What we need is no longer a text generator that only talks a good game, but a "digital engineer" that can truly understand multimodal context and execute with real strength.

Recently, Ant Ling officially open-sourced its latest-generation native multimodal large model, Ling-3.2-air, offering a highly sincere, cost-effective solution to this industry pain point. The model continues the native multimodal architecture of Ling-3.0-flash-VL and fully supports mixed input of text, images, and video. More notably, its underlying architecture makes an extreme trade-off: with a total parameter count of 124 billion, only 5.5 billion parameters are activated per token. This typical MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) sparse activation design aims to use a huge parameter pool to store vast multimodal knowledge while maintaining highly efficient response speeds at extremely low inference cost, truly achieving "large-model intelligence at small-model cost."

The biggest highlight of Ling-3.2-air is its leapfrog reinvention of coding and agent capabilities. Official benchmark data provides highly convincing answers:

- Real-world code repository challenges: In the rigorous SWE-bench Pro evaluation, its score soared from 26.40 in the previous generation to 58.28. This means that when handling bug fixes and feature iterations in complex real-world codebases, its success rate has undergone a qualitative leap of more than doubling, no longer limited to simple single-file-level generation.

- Complex workflow automation: In the AutomationBench-AA (automated workflows) benchmark, its score jumped amazingly from 15.7% to 61%. This marks that the model can now turn vague natural language instructions into stable, coherent multi-step automated execution chains, greatly reducing the chance that agents drop the ball in real business scenarios.

This open-source release from Ant Ling is by no means a simple pile-up of parameters, but a precise calibration of the path to deploying "multimodal + Agent." When a model can simultaneously "see" interface screenshots, "understand" code logic, and "execute" automated workflows, AI can truly evolve from an assistant tool into a core of productivity. With an activation cost of 5.5 billion, Ling-3.2-air delivers results comparable to much larger models, providing developers struggling with compute costs and real-world deployment results a highly cost-effective breakthrough tool.

When multimodal large models are no longer limited to "describing the world" but begin to "reshape the world," the open-source community's next productivity explosion may well be incubating in these models that can solve complex tasks for real.
